AirTag 2 will launch this year with improvements to tracking range and speaker volume. However, one important feature has not been improved: battery life. Fortunately, there's an accessory on the market that can extend the AirTag 2's battery life from about a year to ten years or even longer.

AirTag accessory extends battery life to ten years or more

Among Apple's many battery-powered products, there's a popular one that doesn't let you charge it: the AirTag.

The original AirTag has always been like this, and the AirTag 2 likewise requires a battery replacement roughly once a year.

The AirTag 2's battery life is the same as the previous generation. But there's a third-party accessory on the market that I've personally used and highly recommend, which can dramatically extend battery life from one year to ten years or even longer.

The Elevation Lab AirTag extended battery case essentially turns your AirTag into an "AirTag Max."

You place an AirTag 1 or 2 into the battery case (both models are compatible), add two AA batteries, and the AirTag's battery capacity increases by 14 times.

The design is quite clever and works very well. The only downside is that the case makes the AirTag bulkier. But I've found that most of the time you don't need the AirTag to be that small, so the extra size of the case really isn't an issue.

You can order AirTag battery bundles on Amazon in several different configurations:

Elevation Lab also has a more compact version with a 5-year battery life instead of 10 years. So if the 10-year version is too bulky for you, consider the other option.

A one-year AirTag battery life isn't bad. But if you have many AirTags tracking different items, constantly receiving low-battery notifications is really annoying. If you don't mind the extra bulk of the case, I strongly recommend the Elevation Lab solution.
